# County Armagh

**County Armagh may be Northern Ireland’s smallest county, but the Orchard County delivers some of the biggest experiences. Known for its warm welcome and rich history, Armagh is the perfect place for a short break or a memorable day trip. From exploring sacred sites and historic cathedrals to sampling world-famous cider and outdoor adventures, you’ll quickly feel right at home.**

## St Patrick's Heritage in Armagh

Armagh is famously linked to Saint Patrick, who founded his first stone church here in 445AD. Today, visitors can admire two magnificent cathedrals - [St Patrick’s Roman Catholic Cathedral](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/st-patricks-cathedral-(roman-catholic)/67722101/) with its striking twin spires, and [St Patrick’s Church of Ireland Cathedral](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/st-patricks-church-of-ireland-cathedral/67686101/), standing on the site of the original church. Both reward the climb with sweeping views across the city. Beneath the latter lies a medieval crypt with fascinating stone carvings, a reminder of Armagh’s sacred heritage.

## Things to Do in County Armagh

Wander Armagh’s narrow lanes, tree-lined Mall and vibrant streets filled with cafés, bars and family-friendly restaurants, including favourites like [Uluru](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/uluru-bar-%26-grill/68824101/). Just a short stroll from the city centre, the 300-acre [Palace Demesne](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/the-palace-demesne-public-park/67512101/) offers meadows, gardens, a Green Gym, and a playful Garden of the Senses. Keep your eyes peeled as you walk, the city is dotted with gargoyles, angels and sculptures created by artist Holger Christian Lönze, a modern nod to its sacred past.

## Explore Navan Fort, Lough Neagh and Orchard County Landscapes

Step beyond the city to discover [Navan Fort (Emain Macha)](https://discovernorthernireland.com/listing/navan-fort/68849101/), an ancient ceremonial site and home of the legendary Red Branch Knights. This interactive experience transports you back to the Iron Age and connects you with Ireland’s mythological past.

On the shores of Lough Neagh, explore woodlands, bogs and orchards, or take part in quirky activities like bog snorkelling in summer. Armagh is also renowned as the Orchard County, home to 6,000 acres of apple trees and the famous Bramley Apple. Sample its flavours year-round or visit during the celebrated [Armagh Food and Cider Weekend](https://discovernorthernireland.com/event/armagh-food-and-cider-weekend/83572101/).

## Plan Your Short Break in County Armagh

Whether you’re planning a day trip or an overnight stay from Belfast, Dublin or further afield, County Armagh offers a unique blend of history, culture, food and outdoor adventure. If you're seeking inspiration check out the [accommodation available in Armagh](https://discovernorthernireland.com/destinations/county-armagh/accommodation/), the [top things to see & do](https://discovernorthernireland.com/destinations/county-armagh/activities-and-attractions/) while you're here, and information on [how to get to County Armagh](https://discovernorthernireland.com/destinations/county-armagh/getting-here/). From St Patrick’s legacy to apple orchards in bloom, every visit promises memorable moments and a warm welcome.
